title: HF4359 (2025-2026 Regular): 2024 amendment to definition of trigger activator reenacted, 2024 changes to crime of transferring a firearm to an ineligible person reenacted with amendments, and affirmative defense repealed for transfers of a firearm to an ineligible person by family or household members.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2026-03-13; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/94/2026/0/HF/4359/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version, 2026-03-13. The bill text only cites the 2024 session-law sections it reenacts; their wording is not in the file read. The repealed subdivision (affirmative defense for a family or household member who transferred a firearm under compulsion) appears in the appendix and is described, not quoted.

operative_text:
Section 1 (reenactment of Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 36, section 2): Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 36, section 2, is reenacted retroactively and without interruption from January 1, 2025.
Section 2 (reenactment of Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 36, section 3): Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 36, section 3, is reenacted retroactively and without interruption from August 1, 2024.
Section 3 (repealer, Minn. Stat. 624.7141, subd. 4): Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 624.7141, subdivision 4, is repealed.
